title: What would you want from an AI Trading Assistant?
author: wills_nicht_wissen
selftext:
What would actually make an AI trading assistant useful to you?

Which features would you want most: market analysis, alerts, trade ideas, news summaries, risk analysis, portfolio tracking, or something else?

And what would make you use it regularly instead of just TradingView, your broker or ChatGPT?

Curious what people actually want from something like this.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: The feature I’d use most is a risk-first workflow: let the assistant explain a market setup, then show position sizing, invalidation levels, exposure correlation, and what would change the thesis. That is more useful than another stream of trade ideas. A tool like Marx could fit as the reasoning layer if those assumptions remain visible and testable.

comments.author: the_arthur_adams
comments.body:
For me it'd have to explain *why* it's flagging something instead of just throwing a signal at me. that's the main thing that'd get me using it daily instead of just squinting at TradingView myself. been messing around with [tradibee.com](http://tradibee.com) lately, it does chart upload -> support/resistance and stop loss with the reasoning behind it, which is the part that actually got me to trust it enough to use regularly.

stuff I still don't really trust from ai tools in general - news summaries (always feels laggy/noisy) and auto trade ideas (feels more like a liability than a help tbh). risk analysis + actually explaining the levels is what separates something useful from a gimmick imo.
